report.verdict: Your payment reliability and backend work are easy to spot, and the results back up your senior title. I’d want to talk with you. For Cobalt Pay, I’d still want to know how deeply you’ve worked with PostgreSQL and event-driven systems.
write_up: Your resume makes a strong case for senior backend work! At Tidewater Commerce, you’ve built checkout services, moved production systems to Kubernetes, and led payment failover work. That’s relevant to Cobalt Pay, though the resume doesn’t yet establish two of its technical requirements.

The payment provider failover line is the model: it names the project, your leadership, the team you worked with, and the change in failed checkouts. Your reconciliation work at Cascade Health Systems and your payq project also matter here, but they arrive well after several less relevant activities.

Let’s bring the checkout and reconciliation work forward and make room by trimming a few office activities for this application. Your resume is strong for senior backend roles; for this particular job, add PostgreSQL depth and event-driven work only where you can substantiate them.

cards.line: Wrote the CI pipeline templates in GitHub Actions that cut median build time from 14 minutes to 6
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model for the rest. It connects a tool and deliverable to a before-and-after measure without making a recruiter guess what improved.

cards.line: Built the internal developer portal in React and TypeScript that 140 engineers use to scaffold services
cards.cannot_tell: For a role above senior engineer, a recruiter would also look for a technical decision that shaped the wider engineering system.
